text:
Kendal Daniels appears to be perfectly fine.

A week removed from a scary neck injury that forced him to be stretchered off the field, Daniels came up with a game-sealing fumble recovery Sunday afternoon to lift the Atlanta Falcons past the San Francisco 49ers.

The Falcons were up nine late at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, trying to fend off one last-ditch effort from the 49ers. With less than a minute left, San Francisco tight end George Kittle caught a wide-open pass and was breaking to the middle of the field, seemingly putting the 49ers into scoring position. But Jessie Bates III dove for Kittle's legs and managed to trip him up. As he was stumbling forward, Kittle lost the ball, allowing Daniels to fly in and land on it untouched.

That secured the 29-20 win for the Falcons, and handed the 49ers their first loss of the season.

Daniels ended up leading the Falcons with a career-high 11 total tackles Sunday, nine of which he did by himself. While the fumble recovery was the most important, he was a force for Atlanta's defense all afternoon. He even intercepted Brock Purdy late in the fourth quarter, which was one of four turnovers the Falcons forced Sunday.

Daniels, whom the Falcons took in the fourth round of the NFL Draft out of Oklahoma, is up to 40 total tackles this season.

Sunday's outing came on the heels of a scary injury in their Week 7 matchup with the Chicago Bears. Daniels came flying in to try and tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland, and he remained down on the field for roughly 10 minutes before being carted off.

Days later, Daniels was back at practice and was cleared to return.

"I scared a lot of people," Daniels said, via the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. "It was a scary play. I'm blessed to come out how I did, and it was a bang-bang play, but I'm happy I'm here."

The Falcons (3-4) will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) next week in Florida.

And Daniels, now with his terrifying neck injury behind him, can keep pushing forward in what has been an already impressive rookie campaign.

McCaffrey was hurt after giving the unbeaten Niners an early lead with a 1-yard touchdown leap on fourth down to cap their opening possession.

text:
San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has returned to the game against the Atlanta Falcons after going to the locker room with a thigh injury. He was initially listed as questionable, but he was able to come back on the first drive of the third quarter.

McCaffrey seemed to aggravate his leg during the first quarter, but he went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter before leaving for the locker room. Before going down with the injury, CMC had four carries for 29 yards and one touchdown in the first half. He added a carry for a loss of two yards in the first attempt back from the locker room. He also has three receptions for 45 yards in the air.

So far this season, he has 77 carries for 350 yards and seven touchdowns on the ground, along with 28 receptions for 190 yards in the air through six games.

McCaffrey is a dual-threat running back in quarterback Brock Purdy's offense and a reliable pass catcher. However, the 30-year-old has a history of injuries. The former Comeback Player of the Year had a PCL sprain, which sidelined him for five games in 2024; a pedal Achilles sprain that sidelined him for eight games the same year; a left calf strain that caused him to miss one game in 2023; and a pedal ankle sprain and thigh hamstring strain each sidelined him for five games in 2021.

The 49ers offense is already without wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (IR), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (IR). McCaffrey is a crucial part of this 49ers offense and having him back on the field is great news for the Niners and their fans.

The running back room also includes rookie Kaelon Black and second-year RB Jordan James. Black currently leads the team in carries (11) and rushing yards (60) against Atlanta. McCaffrey leads the team in carries and rushing yards this season, with Black behind him and their QB third on the list.

With the exception of 2024, when he was limited to four games due to injury, McCaffrey has led the team in rushing yards, including two 1,000-plus yard seasons.

In his 10-year career, he has 1,735 rushes for 7,939 yards and 69 rushing touchdowns. McCaffrey was drafted in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, when the Carolina Panthers took him at No. 8 overall. He remained in the Queen City until 2022, when he joined the 49ers.

The Niners are currently down 19-14 against the Falcons as San Fran looks to stay undefeated.

CBS Sports will continue to update this article as more information becomes available.

text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton, in his second game back after returning from offseason blood clot treatment, suffered a fractured fibula in Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and will be out indefinitely.

"TMo is gonna be out for a while," coach Dave Canales said after the game.

Moton was initially considered questionable before being downgraded to out before the end of the third quarter.

Moton pounded the turf while holding his left leg following a Yaya Diaby sack on quarterback Bryce Young with 14:13 left in the third quarter. Trainers immediately ran over to Moton, examined his leg and put him on the back of a cart, which took him into the home tunnel.

First-round pick Monroe Freeling, who had filled in for Moton during the first four games of the season, immediately came in to play right tackle. Left tackle Rasheed Walker gave up a sack to Diaby on the very next play.

Moton, 32, has played just seven quarters of football this season. He has been the Panthers' starting right tackle for the past nine seasons. The 2017 second-round pick is the longest tenured non-specialist on the Panthers' roster.

Moton is signed through the 2028 season. However, 2027 is the final season on his contract with guaranteed money.

The already depleted San Francisco 49ers are dealing with another injury to a key player.

Running back Christian McCaffrey led Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons early due to a thigh injury. McCaffrey went to the locker room after getting his thigh worked on for several moments on the sideline. He did return in the second half, though.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Saturday in advance of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys.

The Eagles ruled four players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Nolan Smith, and Michael Carter II.

Smith missed practice all week due to a hamstring injury while Wicks missed practice all week due to an ankle injury. The Eagles being without their top two wide receivers certainly isn’t ideal. The team will roll with Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, Hollywood Brown, and Britain Covey. The Cowboys’ defense is so bad that these players could still have chances to succeed on Monday night.

Smith missed practice all week while in the concussion protocol. He might be able to return in Week 8.

Carter II has been unavailable since getting injured in Week 5. The Eagles will go with Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean as their top two safeties in base packages with Kenny Moore playing on the back end of the defense in nickel formations.

The Eagles ruled seven players QUESTIONABLE: Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, and Jakorian Bennett.

Barkley was full go on Saturday after being limited on Thursday and Friday. It sure seems like he’s going to give it a go on Monday night.

Dickerson was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Seems like the Eagles will activate him from injured reserve to start at left guard. If so, it will be interesting to see how he fares after he really did not look great in Week 1.

Greenard did not practice on Friday or Saturday after being listed as limited on Thursday. He talked about being a game-time decision. Even if Greenard does suit up, he’ll likely be on a pitch count. Not great.

Hunt was limited in practice all week. With the Eagles looking thin at edge rusher, it would be nice if he can play. We’ll see.

The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Monday to activate any or all of Dickerson, Stowers, Calcaterra, and Bennett from injured reserve in order to play against the Cowboys. The team has some open roster spots to fill, so, we’ll see how they handle things.

Players notably listed without a game status: Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Zack Baun, Hollywood Brown, Jihaad Campbell, Jalen Carter, Britain Covey, Jordan Davis, Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Willie Lampkin, Moro Ojomo, and Tyler Steen.

All of these players were listed on the injury report this week.

Goedert was full go on Saturday after not practicing on Thursday and Friday. With DeVonta and Wicks out, at least Tanner McKee will have the Eagles’ top tight end available to him.

Kendall is set to return to the starting lineup after missing two games. The starting offensive line will look like: LT Jordan Mailata, LG Landon Dickerson (or Willie Lampkin), C Drew Kendall, RG Tyler Steen, RT Markel Bell.

With Nolan Smith out and both Greenard and Hunt questionable, the Eagles only have two edge rushers sure to play on Monday: Ebiketie and Epenesa. The team could also look to temporarily elevate Keyshawn James-Newby to the roster again for more help.

Lamar Jackson’s Injury Status Raises Questions Ahead of Bengals Game

ESPN reported that Lamar Jackson was downgraded to out for the game against the Bengals, meaning Tyler Huntley will start. With Jackson in the final year of his contract, the situation has sparked questions about whether he is healthy enough to play.

Sports Injury Central has anticipated this outcome for weeks. Jackson has a legitimate ankle aversion injury and is not 100%. While he could potentially play from the pocket, that would limit the many facets of his game.

Jackson was compared to a finely tuned Formula One race car rather than a pickup truck. He needs to be closer to 100% to play effectively, particularly because running has been such an important part of his career. A similar situation occurred in 2022 with his knee and ankle.
